title: Successfully demonstrated vehicle-mounted anti-tank guided missile system: Adani Defence

ai.summary: Adani Defence successfully demonstrated a vehicle-mounted anti-tank guided missile system at Pokhran, claiming it meets Indian battlefield needs with features like 8km range, dual-missile engagement, and resistance to electronic jamming.

facts.claim: Adani Defence successfully demonstrated a vehicle-mounted anti-tank guided missile system at Pokhran
facts.quote: Adani Defence and Aerospace has “successfully demonstrated” a vehicle-mounted anti-tank guided missile (ATGM) system at the Pokhran field firing ranges in Rajasthan, the firm shared on Saturday.

facts.claim: The system can engage targets at 8km range with dual-missile capability
facts.quote: Enumerating Bagheera AT1’s features, the company said the anti-tank engagement has a range of 8 km, with the wider missile architecture capable of supporting guided engagements of up to 10 km.

facts.claim: The system uses laser beam for engagement, resistant to electronic jamming
facts.quote: The missile rides a laser beam rather than relying on a radio link, making it highly resistant to electronic jamming on a battlefield increasingly shaped by drones and electronic warfare

facts.claim: The system can fire two missiles in quick succession along the same beam
facts.quote: Two missiles can be fired in quick succession along the same beam at a single target. The first engages the tank’s Active Protection System (APS), while the second is designed to penetrate its defences

facts.claim: The system has 12 missiles per vehicle capacity
facts.quote: Four ready-to-fire missiles on the automated launcher and eight reloads onboard provide a total capacity of 12 missiles per vehicle
